text:
A man is walking through a graveyard when he sees another man squatting next to a grave. "Morning!" he calls out.
"No, just having a shit!"
gist: A man greets someone squatting by a grave with 'Morning!', and the other, hearing 'mourning', says no, he is just relieving himself.

characters.looks: cheerful man walking, waving, coat
man squatting behind gravestone, embarrassed

text:
Got home to find my wife had left a note on the fridge that said "This isn't working I'm going to my mum's"
I opened up the fridge. The light was on and the beer was cold. I'm not sure what she was talking about.
gist: A wife leaves a fridge note saying 'this isn't working', and the husband opens the fridge, finds it cold and lit, and is puzzled.

wordplay.explanation: 'This isn't working' about the relationship versus about the fridge.

characters.looks: man in work clothes, puzzled, holding beer
woman with suitcase, leaving

adaptNote: phrase the note as 'Так больше не работает'

text: My wife screamed in pain during labor so I asked, “What’s wrong?”. She screamed. “These contractions are going to kill me!!” “I am sorry, honey,” I replied. “What is wrong?”
gist: A wife in labor screams that the contractions are killing her, and the husband 'helps' by expanding 'what's' into 'what is'.

wordplay.explanation: 'Contractions' are labor pains and shortened word forms like 'what's'.

characters.looks: nervous husband, scrubs gown, clueless smile
woman in hospital bed, red-faced, screaming

text:
A drunk guy is showing friends his new apartment...
The last stop is the bedroom, where a big brass gong sits next to the bed.
"What's that gong for?" the friend asks him.
"It's not a gong," the drunk replies. "It's a talking clock."
"How does it work?"
The guys picks up a hammer, gives the gong an ear-shattering pound, and steps back.
Suddenly, someone on the other side of the wall screams, "For God's sake, you asshole...it's 3:30 in the god damn morning!"
gist: A drunk shows off a gong as his talking clock, strikes it at night, and an angry neighbor yells the exact time through the wall.

characters.looks: tipsy man, messy hair, untucked shirt, grin
puzzled friend, casual clothes
angry voice behind the wall, pajamas

text:
We are 11 days into self-isolation ands it is really upsetting me to witness my wife standing at the living room window gazing aimlessly into space with tears running down her cheeks.
Don’t get me wrong, I empathize with her.  I’ve considered letting her in many times, but rules are rules.
gist: A husband describes his wife tearfully staring through the window during lockdown, then reveals she is outside and he won't let her in.

characters.looks: man on sofa in sweatpants, mock sympathetic face
woman outside window, tearful, pressed against glass

text:
The kids asked what was for dinner and I told them "Scraps". They started crying. Spoiled brats, it's really hard to get food at the moment thanks to the panic buying.
And it was a stupid name for a dog anyway.
(Obligatory thank-you edit for the silver!)
(Narwhal! Narwhals are cool!)
gist: A parent says dinner is 'Scraps' amid panic-buying shortages and the kids cry, then it turns out Scraps was the family dog.

characters.looks: tired dad in apron at stove, deadpan
crying kids at dinner table
scruffy mutt with name collar

adaptNote: Drop the Reddit edit lines; dog name can be a Russian name meaning scraps.

text:
Boy aged 4: Dad, I’ve decided to get married.
Dad: Wonderful; do you have a girl in mind?!
Boy: Yes... grandma! She said she loves me, I love her, too....and she’s the best cook & story teller in the whole world!
Dad: That’s nice, but we have  a small problem there!
Boy: What problem?!
Dad: She happens to be my mother. How can you marry my mother!
Boy: Why not?! You married mine!
gist: A small boy wants to marry his grandma, and when his father objects she is his mother, the boy points out the father married the boy's mother.

characters.looks: four-year-old boy, earnest face, toy in hand
amused dad, cardigan, coffee mug
kind grandma, apron, glasses

text:
My wife stormed into the pub last night as me and the boys were downing shots of Tequila.
“You’re coming home now!” she screamed.
“No, I’m not,” I laughed.
She said, “I’m talking to the kids.”
gist: A wife storms into a pub demanding 'you're coming home', the man refuses, and she clarifies she meant the kids drinking with him.

characters.looks: cheerful man raising tequila shot
furious woman, hands on hips, coat
young boys at the bar with shot glasses
